verdict.rationale: Proa's own docs show a first-party routing surface built into the framework: routes registered in a generator-maintained `src/routes.rs`, a `proa site routes` route-table command, route specs that accept page caching, and typed route state through WebContext. It is not shown as a standalone, fully documented routing library, and it runs on Axum, a third-party server, so coverage of the story is partial. missing for 10: documentation of routing features in depth (path/query parameters, nested routes, client-side navigation), evidence of a distinct official routing library rather than framework route registration on Axum, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use an official first-party routing library that integrates seamlessly with the framework

citations.quote: Register it in `src/routes.rs`, between the markers the generator maintains
Check the route table: proa site routes
Add page caching to the route spec when the response should carry CDN cache headers.
Every render has typed access to request-scoped data, response metadata, route state, and loader caching through the same WebContext
Go Axum-native for Proa routing and responses
